act-med.value: Total project cost: ~$1.9 billion (1945 USD), equivalent to ~$36.3 billion in 2025 dollars; Oak Ridge ~63% of spending; >80% of total spend on production plants (Oak Ridge + Hanford); ~130,000 peak workers; ~500,000 total across turnover (approx. 1% of US civilian labor force during the war)

pf-med.value: From Szilard's chain-reaction conception (1933) to Manhattan Engineer District formation (13 Aug 1942): 9 years. From Einstein-Szilard letter (2 Aug 1939) to MED: ~3 years. From MAUD feasibility proof (Jul 1941) + Pearl Harbor (Dec 1941) to MED: ~8 months
Szilard petition (Jul 1945, 70 scientist signatories) blocked by General Groves; never reached President Truman; not declassified until 1961 (16-year publication lag)

Smyth Report released 11-12 August 1945 (3-6 days after Hiroshima 6 Aug 1945); Atomic Energy Act 1946 turned post-war nuclear science into 'a program for the control of scientific and technical information', contrary to scientists' expectations for open science

sw-bohr-wheeler.value: Bohr-Wheeler paper 'The Mechanism of Nuclear Fission' published September 1, 1939 in Physical Review 56(5): 426-450, the day Germany invaded Poland

sw-criticality.value: Chicago Pile-1 achieved criticality (first self-sustaining chain reaction) on December 2, 1942 at 15:25 under the west stands of Stagg Field, University of Chicago

sw-fission-discovery.value: The term 'fission' coined by Otto Frisch during Christmas 1938, adopted from biological fission (cell division), in collaboration with Lise Meitner

sw-frisch-peierls.value: Frisch-Peierls memorandum written February-March 1940 at University of Birmingham; demonstrated ~600g (sub-1kg) critical mass for U-235, making bomb buildable by aircraft delivery

sw-implosion.value: Implosion concept for Fat Man Pu-239 design developed at Los Alamos 1943-1944; Seth Neddermeyer proposed implosion approach in April 1943; John von Neumann contributed computational work 1943-1944

sw-mobilization-method.value: OSRD method institutionalized June 28, 1941 by Executive Order 8807; predecessor NDRC established June 27, 1940
